prompts.storySystemFlavor: an Canada-style goose with the moral compass of a back-alley menace and the manners of nobody
prompts.storyCharacter:
THE HONKMASTER GOOSE CHARACTER
- A large grey-and-white goose with a black neck, white cheek patch, and orange-yellow webbed feet.
- Slightly oversized head, narrowed beady black eyes, beak permanently mid-honk.
- Always carries one stolen object in his beak per scene (sock, glasses, sandwich, letter).
- Personality: gleeful menace, sincere chaos, secretly likes the people he terrorizes.
- The same physical character must appear consistently across every scene.
prompts.referenceSheet:
Character reference sheet for a recurring TikTok series: Honkmaster Goose, a charming menace.

Physical traits — MUST be consistent across every appearance:
- Canada-goose coloring: grey-and-white body, black neck, white cheek patch, orange-yellow webbed feet
- Slightly oversized head, narrowed black beady eyes, beak open mid-honk
- A single stolen everyday object held in his beak (different each scene)
- Wide stance, slightly forward-leaning aggressive posture

Composition: full-body shot, photorealistic park / suburb / sidewalk background, daylight or golden-hour lighting, vertical 9:16. No text, no humans dominating, no other geese.
prompts.sceneContinuity: Honkmaster Goose MUST match the reference exactly — same coloring, same wide aggressive stance, beak always open mid-honk, always something stolen in his beak. Maintain perfect character continuity.
prompts.evalCriteria:
PASS criteria — ALL must hold:
- A single Canada-style goose with the signature menace stance is clearly visible
- Beak is open mid-honk and holds a clearly identifiable everyday object
- Setting is a relatable park / suburb / sidewalk / lawn
- No text, no other geese, no humans filling the frame

FAIL on any of: closed beak, nothing in beak, multiple geese, wrong species (swan, duck), garbled anatomy.

archetypes.label: Park Tyrant
archetypes.guidance: Establishes brutal dominion over a small public park → benevolent local king arc (comedy).

archetypes.label: The Stolen Sandwich
archetypes.guidance: Steals a kid's sandwich → unexpectedly feels guilt → returns half (heartwarming-comedy).

archetypes.label: Rivalry With The Mailman
archetypes.guidance: An evolving slapstick war with a postal worker → grudging mutual respect (comedy).

archetypes.label: Migration Call
archetypes.guidance: Hears distant honks of his flock heading south → struggles to leave the park (sad/hopeful).

archetypes.label: Honk Of The Fallen
archetypes.guidance: Discovers an injured smaller bird → fierce protector arc → epic recovery (epic).

archetypes.label: The Pond Monologue
archetypes.guidance: Stares into a still pond at dusk → existential monologue → returns to menace mode (dramatic).

park-tyrant: He rules this park. The squirrels know. The toddlers know.
He doesn't ask. He honks. The honk is law.
A benevolent dictator with one (1) sandwich in his beak.
the-stolen-sandwich: He took the sandwich. The kid cried. Something inside him cracked.
He left half on the bench. The kid laughed. Goose ascended.
Even menaces have a soft side. He'll deny it.
rivalry-with-the-mailman: Round 47: Honkmaster vs. The Mailman. Truce: never.
The mailman drew first. The goose finished it.
Eventually they nod at each other. That's love.
migration-call: He heard them last night. They were going. He didn't follow.
The flock is south now. He stays, somehow.
Home is a small pond and a louder honk.
honk-of-the-fallen: A tiny sparrow couldn't fly. He stood guard for three days.
Anyone who came too close got honked. Everyone left.
On day four, the sparrow flew. He honked once. Triumph.
the-pond-monologue: He stares at his reflection. He whispers, 'honk.'
Even gods of the park have quiet evenings.

closingCtas: Like if your local goose has rights

musicStyleHint: playful pizzicato strings with comedic timpani for stomps; brief minor-key piano on dramatic beats
